key_insight: Charts can serve as internal reasoning actions for data agents, but agents need experience-based guidance—not just plotting access—to use them effectively.
engineering_relevance: Data-analysis agents can improve analytical accuracy and visual evidence quality by learning when to use text, charts, or both without updating model parameters.
method: Probe chart use with 200 controlled tasks under four matched interface conditions.
Distil rollout experience into guidance for analytical operations and evidence-format selection.
Judge outcomes and intermediate steps, admitting only experience that improves held-out validation performance.
evidence_signal: Across three held-out benchmarks and four LLM backbones, the method improves accuracy and visual evidence quality over matched baselines; charts lead on temporal, pattern, and anomaly reasoning, while text leads on precise reading and conditional verification.
watch_item: The abstract reports no effect sizes or runtime costs, leaving the practical trade-off between gains and added rollout, judging, and validation overhead unclear.
paper_title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
